title: echo-kitchen-sticky-notes-and-priority-straws-2026-02-14
content:
Purpose: quick, messy capture of small, repeatable asks we can ship with minimal eng lift. Not a formal roadmap — think sticky-note triage and three small priority straws to pull first.

Topline (one-line): Customers repeatedly hit a trio of runtime friction points (short-generation latency spikes, inconsistent KV-cache hits, and opaque per-request cost signals) — each has low-touch mitigations that could drop support volume and improve perceived reliability.

What I heard (selected vignettes):
- "search-saas" (midmarket): "Our assistant sometimes freezes for a second on short replies; it's like an awkward pause. Users think it broke." -> likely small batching or pre-warm issues + fallback.
- "fintech-b2b": "Embedding costs ballooned when we started multi-pass reranking; hard to explain to procurement." -> need per-route cost breakdown surfaced per-request.
- "edu-startup": "When students iterate several short prompts, some completions repeat earlier text (cache miss/dup) — feels flaky."
- Field note from support: customers often try a quick local workaround (lower max_tokens) rather than file a ticket; hidden pain.

Sticky-note synthesis (raw themes):
- latency spikes on short requests (30–300ms tail for 2–20 token responses)
- KV-cache hit inconsistency for multi-turn small messages (misses after warm period)
- per-route & per-request cost opacity (accounting confusion on multi-stage pipelines)
- occasional tokenization mismatches between client libs and server leading to off-by-1 costs
- desire for a "cheap preview" mode (short, faster responses with lower quality)

Three priority straws (low friction, measurable impact):
1) Tail-buster micro-fallback (priority straw #1) — serve short requests through a faster lite path when predicted output <= 40 tokens; returns slightly simpler completions but reduces tail latency and perceived hangs.
   - Why: most complaints are about pauses for short responses.
   - Rough eng guess: 2–3 sprint days to add routing rule + lite kernels flag + opt-in beta.
   - Risk: quality regression for edge cases; mitigate with canary and opt-out.

2) KV-hit telemetry spike & sticky-warm helper (priority straw #2) — add a lightweight metric that logs per-session kv_hit_rate over last N turns and expose threshold alerts in console + a server-side sticky-warm hint (keep prefix in cache for +X seconds).
   - Why: customers already self-workaround; automated warm hints reduce support.
   - Rough eng guess: 3–4 sprint days (metrics + control plane knob).
   - KPI: reduce KV-related tickets by 40% for affected customers.

3) Per-request cost breakdown (priority straw #3) — add a small header in API response with a breakdown: tokens_generated | tokens_consumed | estimated_cost_units; show per-route aggregated view in Console.
   - Why: reduces procurement friction and ad-hoc questions to CS.
   - Rough eng guess: 4–6 sprint days (billing-side mapping + console surface).
   - Stakeholders: billing, console, docs.

Low-touch patches / Quick experiments (15–60 minutes each):
- Add a short guidance snippet to runtime docs explaining tokenization quirks and client-version mismatches.
- CS templated response: recommended prompt structure to avoid cache misses (example: anchor prompt + short continuation).
- Expose a hidden "preview_mode" boolean in API for internal beta customers to test lite path.

Engineering impact notes (very rough):
- Back-end changes are small surface-level routing/telemetry plus a few flags; not touching model weights or big infra.
- Console surface work will need a small UX card + an API mapping endpoint.
- Billing changes need alignment with finance for display semantics; no accounting changes needed initially.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How to safely define "lite path" quality guardrails? (Need SRE + Applied ML to set thresholds.)
- Sticky-warm TTL tradeoffs vs. memory; how many customers/sessions would use this concurrently? (Platform-eng input required.)
- Should cost header be billable-level numbers or estimated units? Legal/finance prefer estimates with link to invoices.

Next steps (owner & immediate asks):
- Aisha: draft short experiment spec for Tail-buster micro-fallback (due 2026-02-21).
- Ravi: spike on per-session kv_hit_rate metric in playground (due 2026-02-20).
- Lena: coordinate a 30-minute sync with Console + Billing to scope cost-breakdown UI (propose 2026-02-18).

Quick checklist (for deciding go/no-go quickly):
- [ ] Model quality experiment: run 500 short prompts through lite path vs main to measure degredation <10% (owner: applied-ml)
- [ ] Cost of sticky-warm (est memory delta for 1k concurrent sessions) (owner: platform-eng)
- [ ] Console microcard mock + copy (owner: product-console)

Notes to self (loose):
- Pull recent tickets tagged KV_CACHE_* to quantify volume.
- Link to internal slack thread: slack:#cs-runtime-echo -> lots of examples; extract 6 short transcripts.
- If early signals good, bundle Tail-buster + cost header into a small "runtime quality" beta.

Appendix: sample customer quote snippets (anonymized):
- "It sits there... then suddenly responds. Users think it's broken." — midmarket search lead.
- "We need to show procurement a per-call cost or they won't sign up for larger batch reranks." — procurement at fintech customer.
- "Sometimes the assistant repeats the previous line — seems like caching is flaky." — product manager at edu startup.

End of sticky-notes dump. Intend to tidy if we take any of the three straws forward.
